roadmap.goal: Slice 01 of Epic #5585 (US-01, ADO Story #5614): a forecaster opening a delivery's Metrics tab sees a fourth card, 'Epic Size & Count', whose line reads how many epics were in the delivery on each recorded day — derived from `point.featureBreakdown.length` (D3), so the chart has weeks of real history on the day it ships, with no backend change and no migration. The Metrics tab regrids from three cards (with the fever chart spanning the full row) to four cards in a 2x2 layout. DISTILL has ALREADY authored all 13 acceptance scenarios and they are RED right now — 12 failing, 15 pre-existing metrics-tab tests still passing. DELIVER authors NO tests. Every step in this roadmap is 'make these already-written scenarios green against the contracts table DISTILL fixed', touching exactly the two production files the DESIGN Component Decomposition table names for this slice.

maintainer_decisions: Two steps, one phase, split by production file. DESIGN names exactly two files for slice 01 and the 13 scenarios partition cleanly across them (1-8 chart, 9-13 tab layout). A third step would have to either re-open a file the previous step closed or invent scope. Step-to-production-file ratio is 1.0, well inside the <= 2.5 guideline.

Chart first (01-01), wiring second (01-02) — even though the layout tests mock `DeliveryEpicSizeChart` wholesale (DeliverySection.metrics.test.tsx:78-86) and would therefore go green with the throwing scaffold still in place. Chart-first is chosen because the slice's learning hypothesis (does recorded `featureBreakdown` actually carry data?) attaches to the chart and must be settled BEFORE any code is written; if it collapses, slice 01 re-plans into slice 02 and 01-02's regrid would be wasted work.

NO test-authoring step. DISTILL authored all 13 scenarios and ran the fail-for-the-right-reason gate. Per ADR-025 / the slim-crafter scope, DELIVER implements against tests it does not own. Any step here that adds, edits, widens or weakens an assertion in either acceptance file is out of contract — if a test looks wrong, STOP and raise it, do not adjust it.

Interim red is accepted and bounded. After 01-01 the 8 chart scenarios are green and the 5 layout scenarios are still red; after 01-02 the whole suite is green. Per the project's green-before-push rule, commit at 01-01 but do NOT push until 01-02 is green. `pnpm build` + Biome are gated at BOTH steps (they do not depend on the test suite); the full `pnpm test` green gate is asserted at 01-02 only.

The features term is threaded to `MetricsTab` as a PROP, not by giving MetricsTab its own `useTerminology()` call. `DeliverySection.tsx:150` already resolves `featuresTerm`, and its sibling `WorkItemsTab` already receives it as a prop (`DeliverySection.tsx:503`, :533, :542). A second `useTerminology()` call inside the same file would be a second source for one value.

Stryker mutation testing is NOT run at slice 01. The project rule is per-FEATURE, and this component's final shape lands in slice 02 (bar series, left `items` axis, widened `FeatureMetric`); mutating a component that is about to gain half its surface would be re-run wholesale two weeks later. This defers a standing project gate and is flagged for explicit maintainer confirmation rather than assumed.
out_of_scope: Any bar series, any stacking, and the left `items` y-axis. DDD-8 gives slice 01 the composed container with the LINE ONLY, and DISTILL further resolved (feature-delta.md:774-776) that the left/items axis is NOT declared in this slice — an axis with no series is a rendering risk for no gain. Slice 02 adds both together. Scenario 5 pins this: `series` must have length exactly 1 and `mock-bar-plot` must not be in the document.

Every backend file. Zero C#, zero EF migration, zero DTO change, zero `DemoDataService` seeding. The `DeliveryFeatureMetric` / `DeliveryFeatureMetricDto` widening and the DDD-6 null-likelihood 500 fix belong to slice 02.

`DeliveryMetricsHistory.ts`. The `FeatureMetric` model gains `totalItems` and `isUsingDefaultSize` and widens `likelihood` in slice 02 — NOT here. Slice 01's whole selling point (AC-1.6) is that the count is derived from the four fields that are ALREADY recorded. If a step finds itself editing the model, the derivation is wrong.

Any production file other than `DeliveryEpicSizeChart.tsx` and `DeliverySection.tsx`. The DESIGN Component Decomposition table names exactly these two for slice 01. A step that needs a third — `EnlargeableChart.tsx`, `colors.ts`, `TerminologyKeys.ts`, the metrics-history model — is a design escalation: STOP, report it, and let DESIGN re-open the table. Do not add the file.

Any new npm dependency. `@mui/x-charts` is pinned at exactly 9.0.1 and `ChartsContainer` / `BarPlot` / `LinePlot` / dual-axis composition are all verified present at that version (feature-delta.md:531). No upgrade, no second charting library, no pattern/hatching helper.
Editing, adding to, skipping or weakening any scenario in `DeliveryEpicSizeChart.test.tsx` or the `DeliverySection Metrics tab layout` describe block. DISTILL owns them.

Legend click-to-toggle filtering (D8, slice 04), hatched estimated segments (D6, slice 03), the burnup estimated-line visibility fix (D9/S9, slice 05), and the CLI / MCP `lighthouse_delivery_metrics` port (D12/D13, slice 06).

The docs page and the `@screenshot` test. The slice-01 brief defers both to DELIVER *after slice 02*, when the chart has its bars — shipping a screenshot of a line-only chart guarantees regenerating it in a fortnight.

steps.name: Replace the RED scaffold with the composed count-line chart
steps.description:
PREREQUISITE, BEFORE WRITING ANY CODE (slice-01 brief, ~10 min, DISTILL handoff repeats it): on the dogfood instance hit `GET .../deliveries/{id}/metrics-history` for a delivery with weeks of history and confirm `points[].featureBreakdown` is non-empty on the great majority of days. This is the slice's learning hypothesis. If it is mostly empty, D3 collapses — the count becomes a new forward-only field, slice 01 loses its retroactive-history selling point and merges into slice 02. STOP and re-plan rather than writing the chart. Record the observed result in the step log either way; a confirmed premise is evidence, not a formality.

Then replace the body of `Lighthouse.Frontend/src/components/Common/Charts/DeliveryEpicSizeChart.tsx` — delete the `// __SCAFFOLD__` comment block and the `throw new Error("Not yet implemented — RED scaffold")`, and KEEP the exported `DeliveryEpicSizeChartProps { history, featuresTerm?, height? }` signature exactly as it stands: DISTILL fixed it as the contract and both acceptance files import against it.

Shape, copied from the two precedent classes, not invented. Outer shell from `DeliveryBurnupChart.tsx:95-146`: `<Card sx={{ p: 2, borderRadius: 2, height: "100%" }}>` wrapping `<CardContent>` with a `<Typography variant="h6">` title. Chart body from `RefreshHistoryChart.tsx:31-63` (the ADR-122 precedent): a `<ChartsContainer>` taking `dataset` / `xAxis` / `yAxis` / `series` / `height` / `margin` props with `<LinePlot />`, `<MarkPlot />`, `<ChartsXAxis />`, `<ChartsYAxis axisId="count" />` as children.

Honour the contracts table verbatim (feature-delta.md:758-767): dataset rows carry key `epicCount` whose value is `point.featureBreakdown.length`; the single series has `id: "epic-count"`, `type: "line"`, `dataKey: "epicCount"`, `yAxisId: "count"`; the count y-axis is `{ id: "count", position: "right" }`; the x-axis is a band scale addressing the dataset via `dataKey` (e.g. `[{ scaleType: "band", dataKey: "label" }]`) whose label column is `point.date.toLocaleDateString()` — `history.points[].date` is ALREADY a `Date` after `parseDeliveryMetricsHistory`, so do not re-wrap it in `new Date(...)`.

Empty state (scenario 6): when `history.points.length === 0`, return the Card/CardContent shell with the title and the copy `"This chart builds forward from today — no snapshots recorded yet."` — copied verbatim from `DeliveryBurnupChart.tsx:15-16`, em dash included — and return BEFORE constructing `ChartsContainer`; the scenario asserts `chartsContainerMock` was never called, so a container rendered with an empty dataset fails it.

Title (scenario 7): built from the `featuresTerm` prop, e.g. `` `${featuresTerm} Size & Count` ``, with a sensible default when the prop is absent. The chart does NOT call `useTerminology()` itself — the term arrives as a prop (contracts table; resolved open question 2).

D3 caveat (scenario 8): a `<Typography variant="body2" color="text.secondary">` line stating that the count leaves out epics that had no items that day. Must contain the literal substring `no items` (case-insensitive) and must NOT contain the features term — see implementation_notes.

Only the LINE. No `<BarPlot />`, no bar series, no left `items` axis (DDD-8 + resolved open question 1). Run `pnpm vitest run src/components/Common/Charts/DeliveryEpicSizeChart.test.tsx` and expect 8/8 green.

steps.scenario_name: plots one point per recorded day whose value is that day's epic count (AC-1.1) | labels each plotted point with the day it was recorded (AC-1.1) | counts a day's epics from the breakdown recorded on that day (AC-1.6) | draws the count against its own right-hand scale so sizes can share the chart (ADR-122) | renders the count as a line and nothing else until sizes ship (DDD-8) | tells the forecaster the chart builds forward when nothing is recorded yet (AC-1.2) | names the chart after whatever this instance calls its epics (AC-1.5) | says the count leaves out epics that had no items that day (D3 caveat)
steps.implementation_notes:
MOCK-SURFACE COUPLING — the sharpest trap in this step. The test mocks `@mui/x-charts` with exactly eight named exports (DeliveryEpicSizeChart.test.tsx:23-33): ChartsContainer, BarPlot, LinePlot, MarkPlot, ChartsXAxis, ChartsYAxis, ChartsTooltip, ChartsLegend. Importing ANY other name from that barrel — ChartsGrid, ChartsAxisHighlight, ChartsSurface — resolves to `undefined` and React throws on render. Importing from a deep path (`@mui/x-charts/LineChart`, the way `DeliveryBurnupChart.tsx:2` does it) bypasses the mock entirely and drags the real charting engine into jsdom. Import ONLY from the `@mui/x-charts` barrel and ONLY from those eight names. `useTheme` is separately mocked out of `@mui/material` to `testTheme`, so theme-derived colours are fine.

SINGLE-LEAF TERMINOLOGY MATCH — scenario 7 uses `screen.getByText(/Initiative/)`, which THROWS if more than one element matches. Testing-library's default matcher reads each element's direct text-node children, so ancestors do not double-count, but two sibling leaves both containing the term do. The features term must therefore appear in exactly ONE rendered text node: the title. Do not put it in the D3 caveat line, the axis label, or the series `label`. Same rule for scenario 8's `getByText(/no items/i)` — exactly one leaf may carry that phrase. This is a real constraint on the copy, not a style preference.

SCENARIO 5 counts SERIES, not axes — one series only. It says nothing about how many y-axes you declare, but DISTILL resolved open question 1 explicitly: declare only the `count` axis in this slice. Slice 02 adds the left `items` axis with the bars.

The fixtures run through the REAL `parseDeliveryMetricsHistory` (DISTILL's deliberate choice — a shape mismatch fails the test rather than passing against a hand-rolled object), so `history.points[].date` is a `Date` and `featureBreakdown` is the parsed array. Derive the count as `point.featureBreakdown.length` — nothing else.

CI learnings apply (docs/ci-learnings.md — consult it before writing, per CLAUDE.md): pre-apply its rules rather than discovering them in CI. No new SonarQube issues of any severity; if a rule genuinely conflicts with a deliberate choice here, suppress narrowly at the call site with a justification.

EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: this step authors no tests at all — DISTILL owns the acceptance suite and DELIVER's slim-crafter scope forbids widening it — so the Hypothesis/state-delta unit mandate has no surface to apply to. The compensating rigour is DISTILL's own coverage: 13 scenarios over 6 ACs with zero uncovered AC, fixtures built through the production boundary parser, and a passed fail-for-the-right-reason gate.

steps.description:
Production change confined to `Lighthouse.Frontend/src/pages/Portfolios/Detail/Components/DeliveryGrid/DeliverySection.tsx`, in and around the `MetricsTab` sibling component at :577-624.

Four edits, all of them small.

(1) Add `data-testid="delivery-metrics-grid"` to the grid `Box` at :592-601 — the one already carrying `gridTemplateColumns: METRICS_GRID_COLUMNS`. Scenarios 10 and 11 address the grid through this testid; it does not exist today, which is exactly why they fail with `Unable to find an element by: [data-testid="delivery-metrics-grid"]`.

(2) Insert the new card THIRD, between the predictability `EnlargeableChart` (:608-613) and the fever chart, as a direct child of the grid Box, following the shape of its three siblings: `<EnlargeableChart ariaLabel="…" render={(height) => <DeliveryEpicSizeChart history={history} featuresTerm={featuresTerm} height={height} />} />`. Import the default export from `../../../../../components/Common/Charts/DeliveryEpicSizeChart` — the path the test's `vi.mock` at :78-86 already targets.

(3) DELETE the fever chart's wrapper `Box sx={{ gridColumn: { lg: "1 / -1" } }}` at :614 and :621, promoting its `EnlargeableChart` to a direct grid child. The contracts table is explicit: this Box is deleted, not re-styled. Scenario 11 asserts the grid has exactly `CARD_ORDER.length` (4) direct children and scenario 10 walks `grid.children` in order expecting burnup, predictability, epic-size, fever — a surviving wrapper Box leaves the child count right but is the thing the AC exists to remove.

(4) Thread the features term. `MetricsTab` currently receives only `{ isLoading, history }` (:577-582). `DeliverySection` already resolves `featuresTerm` at :150. Add `featuresTerm: string` to `MetricsTabProps`, destructure it, and pass it at the call site (:508-512) — precisely the way `WorkItemsTab` is already fed the same value at :503. Scenario 13 asserts the chart mock was called with `expect.objectContaining({ featuresTerm: "Epics" })`.

Do NOT touch `METRICS_GRID_COLUMNS` (:575). It is already `{ xs: "1fr", lg: "1fr 1fr" }`; DISTILL extracted it so scenario 12 could assert the configuration value, and that scenario passes today as a regression guard. Changing it breaks a green test.

Then run the full frontend gate and the dogfood moment: open the dogfood instance's longest-running delivery, Metrics tab, confirm the line already shows weeks of history and that the 2x2 grid matches the ADO 5585 sketch — then narrow the viewport, because AC-1.4's responsive behaviour is the one thing jsdom cannot observe.

steps.scenario_name: shows the epic size and count card built from the same fetched history (AC-1.3) | reads the four cards burnup, predictability, epic size and count, fever (AC-1.3) | gives each of the four cards its own cell so none spans the whole row (AC-1.3) | pairs the cards on a wide screen and stacks them on a narrow one (AC-1.4) | hands the chart this instance's word for epics (AC-1.5)
steps.implementation_notes:
These five scenarios mock `DeliveryEpicSizeChart` wholesale (test :78-86), so they exercise the WIRING only and would pass even against the throwing scaffold. That is not licence to reorder the steps — see maintainer_decisions — but it does mean a failure here is always a wiring bug, never a chart bug. Debug accordingly.

Scenario 10 uses `child.querySelector('[data-testid="…"]')`, which searches DESCENDANTS and not the child element itself. Each grid child must therefore be a wrapper containing the chart testid below it — which is what `EnlargeableChart` already gives you for the three existing cards. Do not flatten the new card into a bare `<DeliveryEpicSizeChart>` as a direct grid child; wrap it in `EnlargeableChart` like its siblings (Reuse Analysis: EXTEND, wrap as-is).

`toHaveBeenCalledWith(expect.objectContaining({...}))` requires the component to be called with exactly ONE argument, which the test's own mock wrapper guarantees. `objectContaining` tolerates the extra `height` that `EnlargeableChart`'s render prop supplies, so passing `height={height}` is safe and matches the siblings.

Threading the prop is the chosen answer to DISTILL's resolved open question 2 (feature-delta.md:777-780) — MetricsTab gets `featuresTerm` from its parent rather than its own `useTerminology()` call, because `DeliverySection` already resolves it at :150 and `WorkItemsTab` already takes it as a prop at :503/:533/:542. A second hook call in the same file would be a second source for one value.

D11 holds: premium gating and RBAC are inherited. The Metrics tab is already behind the premium check and the portfolio's RBAC read guard — add no gate, and do not let the fourth card acquire one by accident.

EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: no tests are authored in this step; the acceptance scenarios are DISTILL's and are already on disk. The compensating rigour is the driving-port coverage DISTILL recorded — the real component tree is rendered and the real tab is clicked, so this is wiring verified through the actual UI port rather than through a unit seam.
